> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **2** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **16** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 157051ceb48d2d9ed289f21f7018a39ce7249178` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `7d00df958ba7e4346b2f2a123f54fa1fecb8839a` — the merge of head `83947aaf59c1d779154afe7904346be05a4a0111` into base `157051ceb48d2d9ed289f21f7018a39ce7249178`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 7d00df958ba7e4346b2f2a123f54fa1fecb8839a && git checkout 7d00df958ba7e4346b2f2a123f54fa1fecb8839a
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 157051ceb48d2d9ed289f21f7018a39ce7249178 83947aaf59c1d779154afe7904346be05a4a0111 && git checkout -B drift-repro 157051ceb48d2d9ed289f21f7018a39ce7249178 && git merge --no-ff 83947aaf59c1d779154afe7904346be05a4a0111

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 157051ceb48d2d9ed289f21f7018a39ce7249178
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 157051ceb48d2d9ed289f21f7018a39ce7249178` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `f64ffdce9f037a47848bc6d706ef233bafa29f7f`
Local-runs: none
Scope: none (the file list decides no schema or governed-path face; `record-recognisers --paths` answers "the paths decide no face") + `packages/metadata/src/metadata-manager.ts`, `packages/metadata/src/loaders/database-loader.test.ts`, `packages/objectql/src/plugin-late-bridge-environment-row.test.ts`, `.changeset/33003-environment-row-rewrite-keeps-mark.md`

PR #33036, card #33003 (p0 for the 18.4.0 window). Inputs: the card and its four comments, the PR body, file list and net diff at this head, the head's check-runs. Read, never run: the head's `metadata-manager.ts`, `plugin.ts` (metadata and objectql), `database-loader.ts`, the protocol's `withRowBinding`, and the `@objectstack/metadata@18.3.0` tag for the released behaviour.

Findings: 0 must-fix, 3 should-fix, 2 nits.

### ① Derived judgments

The four writes the brief names, judged on the tree:

| write | call on the manager | in process | after a reboot from the same database |
|---|---|---|---|
| bridge re-register (`ownPreviousCopy`) | `register('object', name, merged, { notify: false })`, `merged._packageId` = HOST | kept | kept |
| bridge restore (`restoreExtendedObjectCopies`) | `register('object', name, served, { notify: false })` | kept | kept |
| `publishPackage(HOST)` | `register(type, name, { ...item.data, publishedDefinition, … })` | kept | kept |
| `revertPackage(HOST)` | `register(type, name, { ...item.data, metadata: clone(publishedDefinition), … })` | kept | kept |

- **In process.** `writeRegistryEntry` reads `typeStore.get(key)` before the `set`. `rewritesEnvironmentRow(before, data)` is true when `before` is in `storedEnvironmentRows` and names its package by `_packageId` alone, and `data` is another object, not in `loadedFrom`, with the same `_packageId`. `data` then joins the set, and `unregisterPackage` skips it at `isStampedEnvironmentRow`. All four copies are spreads of the marked entry (or ObjectQL's merged object), so all four qualify. The registry entry keeps `_packageId`, so the bridge's own `existing._packageId === obj._packageId` test and ObjectQL's owner still read HOST.
- **After a reboot.** `register` computes `environmentRowStamp(data)` after the registry write and hands `loader.save` a copy without the top-level `_packageId`, and without `metadata._packageId` when it equals the stamp. The row's `package_id` column stays empty for a non-slotted type. At the next boot `loadMany` reads `indexedItemPackageId(item) === undefined`, marks the row again, and the pass re-stamps it. `storedItemPackageId` peels to the `metadata` body when a row has one, which is why the revert case needs the body strip. `publishedDefinition` keeps a nested `_packageId`; no package read looks there.
- **The host's own rows are still removed.** A row whose stored body carries `_packageId: HOST` is not marked by `loadMany`, so no copy of it is marked and its body is stored as given. A copy that names the host by `packageId` or `package` fails `isStampedEnvironmentRow` at each use. A loader-handed item is never treated as a copy (`loadedFrom`). One exception is nit N2.
- **#32999's guard holds.** The `loadMany` mark, `isStampedEnvironmentRow` and the `unregisterPackage` skip are unchanged; the diff only adds members to the set and reads it at `register`. A second pass over a marked entry is still decided by `loadMany`, not by the carry.
- **Other writers.** The choke point covers every `register` / `registerInMemory` caller, including `bulkRegister` and both `importMetadata` arms, the ObjectQL object-copy follow and the artifact sink. `rollback` is the one writer that reaches neither half for storage: see S2.
- **Pins under ablation, by reading.** Metadata suite, 22 cases:
  - A, carry removed: the copy is unmarked, so the six in-process pins lose the row; `environmentRowStamp` is then undefined, the stamp is stored, and the five persisting writers' reboot pins go red. The `registerInMemory` reboot case and the CONTROLs stay green. 11 red is consistent.
  - B, stamped body saved: only the five reboot pins.
  - C, body strip removed: only publish-then-revert after a reboot.
  - D, `loadedFrom` test removed: the re-saved-row CONTROL (a loader-handed stamped row would inherit the mark).
  - E, stamp equality removed: the other-package CONTROL.
  - ObjectQL suite: it drives the plugin's real `bridgeManifestObjectsToMetadataService` and `restoreExtendedObjectCopies` over a real registry and `DatabaseLoader`, and asserts both processes. Sound.
- **Check-runs on this head:** 24 success, 16 skipped, 9 in progress (`Test Core` 1/8 to 8/8, `Type Check · workspace`). `Check Changeset`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard` and the PR-body guards are green. This verdict is by reading; landing still needs every check green.

### ② Semver level

`@objectstack/metadata: patch`, `Metadata-protocol: none`, `Clause-②: no`. Correct: a defect fix, no authorable key, value or type moves, and the only non-test source file is in `packages/metadata`. `@objectstack/objectql` gains a test file only, so it needs no entry. The changeset text matches the tree: the six writers, the mark carry, the two strip positions, the unchanged cases. One omission: S1.

### ③ Boundary flags

**The open question (comment 6845180542): option A. `Clause-②: no` stands; not a must-fix.**

The declaration asks whether a published package's accept set or public surface widens or narrows (CONTRIBUTING.md item 5). Nothing a caller can pass or call changes. What moves is one private provenance key in the stored body of one class of rows. Reader by reader:

- **The next boot pass.** It reads the rewritten row package-less, marks it and re-stamps it with the declared host. The registry entry is the one `main` produced (`_packageId: HOST`). The only difference is the edge the dev names: a host that stops declaring, or changes, its package between boots reads the row package-less where the persisted stamp used to answer. That is what every unrewritten row answers already.
- **History snapshots.** `save` hands `createHistoryRecord` the same stripped body, so versions written by a rewrite no longer hold `_packageId`. A `rollback` to one restores a stamp-less body, which is what a rollback to an authored version restores. No door's answer depends on the key being there.
- **Direct `sys_metadata` readers.** The protocol states a stored row's package from the `package_id` column only: `withRowBinding` replaces a body's `_packageId` with the column's package, or drops it for a package-less row. A body stamp on a non-slotted row was never served, so nothing moves.
- **Export.** `exportMetadata` reads `list`, where the registry entry (stamp kept) wins over the loader's copy. Unchanged.
- **Against 18.3.0.** Its `unregisterPackage` matched `packageId` / `package` only, so it kept these rows; this head keeps them.

The stored-body difference is disclosed in the PR body and the changeset says where the stamp is no longer stored. That is enough for `no`.

Should-fix:

- **S1. Rows already stored with the stamp by 18.3.0 and earlier are outside this fix and #32999, and the changeset does not say so.** In `@objectstack/metadata@18.3.0`, `_loadFromFileSystem` registers each loaded item with `{ notify: false }` and no `skipSourceLoader` (that option landed after the 18.3.0 tag, #31699 R5-A). `register` then calls `loader.save` with the body the pass has just stamped, and `storedBodyUnchanged` hashes the whole body, so the row is rewritten with `_packageId: HOST`. So wherever that boot pass stamped a stored row, it also stored the stamp, for every such row and not only for the two writes the card names. On a database upgraded from 18.3.0 those rows are read as the host's own (this PR's own CONTROL pins that byte state as "removed"), and `unregisterPackage(HOST)` deletes them once #32198 ships. `migrateDatabaseLoaderRowPackages` covers slotted types only. This is not a defect of this diff; the dev's "same bytes" argument explains why no boot rule can tell the two apart. It does bear on the release decision the card carries: #32986 and #33003 protect a fresh database and rows created after the upgrade. Owed: a card for the upgrade path, graded with #32198's release line, and one changeset sentence saying a row whose stored body already carries the host stamp is treated as the host's. Read from the tag, not run.
- **S2. `rollback` is an unmeasured writer.** It persists through `dbLoader.registerRollback`, not `register`, then calls `writeRegistryEntry(type, name, restoredMetadata)`. Restoring a snapshot that carries `_packageId: HOST` (any version written by a rewrite before this PR) marks the entry in process but stores the stamp, so the row is the host's after a reboot. No in-repo caller; it is a public method of the manager. Owed: a row in the writers table, plus either the strip on that path or a follow-up card.
- **S3. The mark does not survive an unstamped replacement followed by a host-stamped copy.** `importMetadata` without `merge`, `bulkRegister` or `rollback` to an authored version replaces the marked entry with an unstamped, unmarked body. That is harmless alone. When ObjectQL's object-copy follow then writes `registerInMemory('object', name, body)` stamped with a registry owner that is still HOST, `before` is unmarked, the entry reads as the host's, and `unregisterPackage(HOST)` in that process deletes the stored row. A reboot restores the protection. Not pinned and not in the FROM → TO table. Owed: a pin for the chain, or a follow-up card that names it. The owner stamp at that moment was read, not exercised.

Author: PR `user.login` is the relay; nothing to name.

### ④ Design judgment

- **The route is right.** Membership alone cannot pass the reboot pin, because a stamped stored body is indistinguishable from the host's own seeded row. Doing both halves at `writeRegistryEntry` / `register`, rather than in each writer, also covers `importMetadata` merge and any future caller.
- **Keeping the stamp on the registry entry is necessary.** The bridge's `ownPreviousCopy` test and `restoreExtendedObjectCopies` both read `existing._packageId` from the service, so stripping it in memory would stop the bridge after the first rewrite.
- **The narrow carry is a deliberate trade.** Requiring the same stamp keeps "a copy stamped with another package is that package's" (CONTROL E). The cost is S3.
- **N1 (nit).** Only `_packageId` is stripped. The pass also stamps `_packageVersion` and `_provenance: 'package'`, and a rewritten row now stores those two without `_packageId`. So the PR body's "the byte state of an environment row nothing has rewritten" is not exact. No reader moves: `applyProtection` fills only unset keys, and the protocol overwrites provenance on read.
- **N2 (nit).** `rewritesEnvironmentRow` tests "not loader-handed and same stamp", not "derived from `before`". A host item of the same name registered over a marked row by a non-loader path (an artifact reload, a code-declared `datasource`) inherits the mark and is kept on unregister. It needs a name collision, where `main` already overwrites the environment's body, and it errs toward keeping.

**VERDICT: PASS**

|---|---|---|

The changeset carries the known-limitation sentence: a row whose stored body already carries the host stamp "reads as the host's own row and is still removed with it … Its upgrade path is #33043". Read on the tree:

The later `writeRegistryEntry` call runs the carry again on the same object, which changes nothing. The host's own row is not marked, so its restored body is stored as given.

The `loadedFrom` test is still the first line of the carry, so a re-read stored row is decided by `loadMany` alone. - **New pins, by reading.**
  - Two S3 chains (`importMetadata` overwrite, `bulkRegister`, each followed by a host-stamped `registerInMemory`): red when the carry is limited to an equal stamp.
  - The rollback pin: red after the reboot when `registerRollback` gets the restored body as is.
  - The rollback CONTROL: seeds stamped rows, so nothing is marked and the row is removed.
  - The claimed counts (26 cases; A 14 red, S2 1 red) are consistent with the code.
  - The S3 chain through `rollback` to an authored version is covered by the same function but has no pin of its own.
- **Check-runs on this head:** 37 success, 18 skipped, none pending or failed. The PR is still a draft.

### ② Semver level

### ③ Boundary flags

`Clause-②: no` still holds. The hop adds no export, option or accepted input. It extends the same stored-body rule to one more write path (`rollback`) and widens an in-process mark. The reader-by-reader answer of the first record is unchanged: the boot pass, history snapshots, the protocol's column-only package read and export answer as before.

Author: PR `user.login` is the relay; nothing to name.

### ④ Design judgment

- Remembering the host per row is the smallest change that closes S3 without giving up CONTROL E. The alternative, marking by name, would have needed a clear on delete.
- Doing the strip inside `rollback` rather than in `DatabaseLoader.registerRollback` keeps the loader ignorant of the mark, as `register` already does.
- **N3 (new nit).** A copy that names the host by its own `packageId` now inherits the mark too, because its `_packageId` equals the host. It is still removed (`isStampedEnvironmentRow` reads every key), but a later stamp-only copy over it becomes the environment's row again and is stored without the stamp. At `f64ffdce` that chain stayed the host's. It needs a writer that first claims an environment row for the host by `packageId`, which only the CONTROL does today, and it errs toward keeping. Not pinned.
